correctness.rationale: For every integer m>=3, exact quotient B_m gives the cubic f_m and cofactor residue x(x-m+2)/f_m; signs bracket three distinct roots. Two roots converge at rate O(1/m) to (-1±sqrt5)/2, the marked projector weights converge to (1±1/sqrt5)/2, and the high spectral mass is O(1/m). Reverse triangle inequality gives a uniform-in-time upper bound for the marked modulus difference. A fixed t=pi/sqrt5 produces the matching lower bound. On all other core pairs an explicit decomposition gives uniform upper bounds O(1/m) or O(1/sqrt m), completing the global maximum claim. Symbolic identities and finite direct-matrix exponentials were checked independently. All m>=3, the time half-line, normalization, and asymptotic domain are explicit; finite tests are not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Actual public-text inspection identifies an explicit induced-subgraph amplitude-stability problem (arXiv:2312.06906v1, Section 12) and shows that its proved 2/m join bound does not apply to a one-edge pendant extension. The independent all-m sharp positive limit, fixed witness, and stability of every other core entry are not given by the inspected spectral general method (arXiv:2208.08971v1) or later normalized-operator clique-localization results (arXiv:2603.05643v1). Targeted published-result and alias searches identify no stronger coverage; this is provisional same-model originality only, not a global novelty certificate.

value.rationale: The exact nonzero limiting defect directly answers a natural counterexample direction to Kirkland–Monterde Section 12, which asks for quantitative stability for general induced graphs with the complete graph explicitly named. A sharp constant 1-1/sqrt5, convergence rate, fixed witnessing time, and the asymmetry that every nonmarked core entry does converge uniformly supply structural information beyond a routine small-graph spectral calculation. The result warns against extrapolating the prior O(1/m) join theorem outside its hypotheses and gives a motivated stability benchmark.
